A series of workshop sessions were completed to discuss the detailed data elements outlined in the OSI DER workbook and how the project solution architecture intersects with the software configuration capabilities. Preliminary models of the DERs and utility usage for the Citizens West complex have been created, and these models provide representative usage characteristics of various DERs including Solar, HVAC, and other energy consumption for a similar complex. Concurrently, additional preliminary designs of optimization techniques for peak load management have been completed incorporating the model for control of stationary storage and EV batteries combined with representative usage of other DERs to maximize grid utilization while minimizing peak demands. Initial demand response optimization-based strategies have been developed to incorporate signals from the utility to lower or increase demand on the grid during defined windows. Additionally, investigation is ongoing into high- and mid- fidelity models of DERs for facility control. 8 6.1.1.2 Subtask 1.2.0: Compile DER Inventory and AMI Installation Schedule DER Device List. PacifiCorp and the project team completed a detailed DER device list for all existing and installed DERs that are available for integration in the project. This list includes over 500 existing DER devices including some DERs that were planned for replacement or additional control upgrades to meet the planned control strategies defined for UDERMS. PacifiCorp and project team members compiled the known DER information and augmented that information with additional details via initial site assessments. The site assessments provided specific DER details including nameplate information, electrical connections, type of EVSE, model numbers, serial numbers, communication identifiers, and specifics for any associated systems (i.e., mini-split HVAC, ducted split systems, etc.). Through this process the project team identified updates to the DER installations and specifics that were not detailed in other building models or diagrams. PacifiCorp also included the associated meter number for each DER in the DER device list as this is needed for multiple tasks and evaluation in the future. AMI Installation. PacifiCorp also worked with the PacifiCorp electric meter operations group to ensure that the known and installed participating facilities were on the AMI meter deployment schedule. As of December 31, 2023, all installed and known controllable DERs and the associated main facility meters have been replaced with AMI meters and programmed to collect 15-minute interval data. This was a significant effort that also included evaluation of data to ensure that the data intervals and reporting were as expected. Additional metering deployments were planned for additional DER device installations (i.e., smart thermostat deployments) or for newly identified evaluation, measurement, and verification requirements. 6.1.1.3 Subtask 1.3.0: Model Distribution Grid Needs Mapping Electrical Pathways. PacifiCorp has worked with the distribution engineering department to extract the relevant distribution network model for each project location so that they can be analyzed by the project team.
